    Gibbs Sampler for Multivariate Regression with Covariance Option

    gibbs_sampler_one_draw_cov.Rd

    This function performs a single Gibbs sampling draw for a multivariate regression model with an option to use either a dense or diagonal covariance matrix for the outcomes. Each outcome has its own set of predictors.

    gibbs_sampler_one_draw_cov(
  y_list,
  X_list,
  sigma_param,
  covariance_type = "diagonal"
)

    Arguments

    y_list

    A list of outcome vectors. Each element \(y_j\) in the list corresponds to the outcomes for one dependent variable.

    X_list

    A list of predictor matrices. Each element \(X_j\) in the list corresponds to the predictor matrix for the corresponding outcome \(y_j\).

    sigma_param

    A list of initial values for the residual variances \(\sigma^2_j\) for each outcome when covariance_type = "diagonal", or a dense covariance matrix when covariance_type = "dense".

    covariance_type

    A string specifying the type of covariance matrix to use. Can be either "diagonal" (no correlation between outcomes) or "dense" (allows correlation between outcomes).

    Value

    A list with the following elements:

    beta_samples

    A list of sampled regression coefficients \(\beta_j\) for each outcome.

    sigma2_samples

    A list of sampled residual variances \(\sigma^2_j\) for each outcome (diagonal case), or the sampled covariance matrix \(\Sigma\) (dense case).

    residuals

    A list of residuals for each outcome \(r_j = y_j - X_j \beta_j\).

    Details

    The model assumes that each outcome \(y_j\) follows a regression model: $$y_j = X_j \beta_j + \epsilon_j, \quad \epsilon_j \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma)$$ where \(X_j\) is the predictor matrix for outcome \(y_j\), \(\beta_j\) is the vector of regression coefficients, and \(\Sigma\) is the covariance matrix of the residuals. The covariance matrix can either be diagonal (independent outcomes) or dense (allowing correlation between outcomes).

    Examples

    # Simulate data for two outcomes with different predictor matrices
set.seed(123)
n <- 100  # Number of observations
p <- 2    # Number of outcomes

# Create predictor matrices X for each outcome
X1 <- cbind(1, rnorm(n))
X2 <- cbind(1, rnorm(n), rnorm(n))

# True beta values
beta1 <- c(1, 0.5)
beta2 <- c(1, -0.3, 0.2)

# Simulate outcomes
y1 <- X1 %*% beta1 + rnorm(n)
y2 <- X2 %*% beta2 + rnorm(n)

# Prepare data for the Gibbs sampler
y_list <- list(y1, y2)
X_list <- list(X1, X2)
sigma_param <- list(1, 1)  # Diagonal case: Initial values for sigma^2

# Run the Gibbs sampler with diagonal covariance
result_diag <-
    gibbs_sampler_one_draw_cov(y_list, X_list,
                              sigma_param,
                              covariance_type = "diagonal")
print(result_diag)

    gibbs_sampler_one_draw_cov(y_list, X_list,
                              sigma_param_dense,
                              covariance_type = "dense")
print(result_dense)
